title: Windshield Frame Sealing Land — Corrosion Repair and Spar Cap Local Reinforcement
abstract: Repair of corrosion in the windshield frame sealing land and local reinforcement of the lower sill spar cap, applied when a windshield is removed and the exposed land is found pitted at the drain path.

sections.purpose: This repair removes corrosion from the windshield frame sealing land, restores the sealing surface flatness and, where the loss reaches the lower sill, reinforces the spar cap locally so that the frame retains its bending capability.
sections.damage_assessment: The land can only be assessed with the windshield removed. Clean off the old sealant with a plastic scraper and inspect the full perimeter, paying particular attention to the lower sill where the frame drain path discharges. Measure the depth of every pit with the depth gauge and record it on the land map. Loss up to 8 per cent of the land thickness may be blended and left. Loss between 8 and 20 per cent needs the local reinforcement of this repair. Loss above 20 per cent, or corrosion that reaches the fastener holes of the splice plate, is outside scope and requires an engineering assessment before a windshield is refitted.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend the corrosion out with a rotary file and progressively finer abrasive, keeping the blend shallow and the edges faired at a ratio of 20 to 1. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area. Measure the remaining land thickness at eight points around the perimeter and record them on the land map. Where the loss at the lower sill is between 8 and 20 per cent, fit the local reinforcement to the spar cap D5610115011532 using the layout on repair drawing RD-56-10-11-906, drilling through the existing pattern only. Where the splice plate D5610114829453 has been disturbed, refit it with new blind rivets AES757493-5D. Apply the chromate-free surface protection to all bare metal and let it cure fully. Check the land flatness with the straight edge and the feeler set; the land must be within 0.15 millimetres over any 100 millimetre length. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the drain path before the windshield is refitted.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is not life limited but the repaired land must be re-inspected at every subsequent windshield removal, and in any case within 8000 flight hours. Do a detailed visual inspection of the perimeter through the internal trim at every C check, looking for sealant lifting at the lower sill, which is the first sign that the land is corroding again. Report the repair with the land map so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Land thickness loss up to 20 per cent over a length not exceeding 150 millimetres, not reaching the splice plate fastener holes and not present on more than one side of the frame.

materials.description: SPAR CAP, WINDSHIELD ASSEMBLY, KIT, FWD

type_data.fastener_pattern: Existing splice plate pattern retained; reinforcement fastened through the existing holes with 36 blind rivets AES757493-5D
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited; re-inspect the land at every windshield removal and in any case within 8000 flight hours.
